summary: Our project explores the science and safety of combustion in microgravity during space exploration. To address the challenge of understanding fire behavior and improving energy efficiency, we developed a AI powered dashboard based on experimental NASA PSI combustion data. Studying flames without the interference of gravity and turbulence allows scientists to observe combustion with high precision, revealing that fire in space can burn at lower temperatures and spread invisibly depending on spacecraft ventilation. This work is vital because its findings directly improve safety and sustainability: on Earth, it supports cleaner fuel burning and has inspired life-saving technologies like smoke detectors and firefighter oxygen tanks, while in space, accurate fire-behavior data is essential to protect astronauts on future long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
Ask Kali !

Ask Kali is a bot/AI that works offline via the built-in PSI Scientific Retrieval & Synthesis Engine as a simple search bot. Optionally, by adding a Google Gemini API key in the Engine tab of the chat window, you can use gemini-3.8-flash for generative LLM synthesis grounded on matched PSI records, turning Ask Kali into a fully featured AI capable of reasoning, searching, context understanding and file output such as CSV and PDF, giving a filtered list of applicable results from NASA’s PSI Data Repository.

Impacts and benefits

With the development of the AstroKali Project, we anticipate that the “Ask Kali !” bot will make the process of searching for documentation based on specific data and metrics far more interactive. It will allow users to retrieve precise information or obtain comprehensive answers with broader suggestions, thereby expanding the possibilities for developing new technologies within the field of combustion science and even apply the results of new and previous studies to fire safety technologies and techniques that we use in our lives.

Besides this, by simplifying the documentation search process with a more streamlined documentation search tool, it is expected that these documents can be reviewed by students and professors, paving the way for scientific research in the field of microgravity combustion and potentially other topics by improving access to documentation on official NASA experiments that might otherwise appear difficult to obtain.

Tools used

  • Antigravity IDE to pull the PSI API dabatabase using Python and JSON;
  • Figma with AI chatbot to code the site design using HTML, CSS and JS;
  • The presentation was made at Canva and the Logo was made with AI using a real photo reference;
  • All the data was storage at a Github repository and the site was uploaded by Github pages, using yaml.
